newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's GDP grew 2.9 pct in January-Sept.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's GDP grew 2.9 pct in January-Sept.

text.p: Colombia's gross domestic product grew by 2.4 percent in the third quarter of 1996, bringing accumulated growth during the first nine months of the year to 2.9 percent, the presidential press office said.

The figure is down from 3.4 percent GDP growth in the third quarter of 1995, but the press office quoted the National Planning Department as saying it represented a slight recovery from the second quarter, when growth totalled just 2.2 percent.

The statement from the press office said the third quarter figures indicated that Colombia would post GDP growth of about 3.0 percent for the entire year, down from the Finance Ministry's latest target of 3.5 percent.

The economic crisis stemming from charges that President Ernesto Samper used drug money to finance his 1994 election campaign weighed heavily on the economy earlier this year, as have high interest rates and cyclical factors led by a sharp slowdown in the contruction industry.
